Job Details:

Job Description:
Analytical Chemistry Lab Engineer

The Analytical Chemistry Lab engineer will work with the Lab technicians and the Lab manager in support of Intel Israel site manufacturing operations.

Your responsibilities will include but not be limited to:
Preparing chemical analysis methodologies in a semiconductor fab environment and incoming raw materials quality control.
Supporting the development of advanced analytical chemistry technology to fulfil next-generation requirements.
Employing chemical analysis expertise in assisting factory engineers on event prevention, root cause clarification and trouble shooting.
Driving lab systems engineering including the development of solutions to improve lab quality, compliance, and throughput.
Driving monitoring, record keeping, and reporting for lab equipment including maintenance, service, calibration, and testing activities.
Assisting and providing mentorship of lab technicians to drive lab execution including engineering analysis, instrumentation, data analysis, and result reporting.
Resolving reported bugs and root causes issues that could impact product quality and experience.
Ensuring lab preparedness including bench setup, procurement of test equipment and other lab materials, and infrastructure requirements.
Collaborating with functional teams such as IT, security, and facilities to maintain a successful lab. Develops and coordinates the design, development, and implementation of new ideas, processes, and systems for lab improvements needed to meet program deliverables.

The ideal candidate should exhibit the following behavioral traits:
Be able to work in a dynamic environment and adapt to fast-changing priorities
A demonstrated ability to work both independently and in a team setting.
Is willing to successfully work as a team with peers, technicians, and other analytical lab groups.
Comfort working with a variety of chemicals including acids, bases, oxidizers, solvents, etc.
Ability to work in a cleanroom environment for several hours each day
Ability to work standing (e.g. at fume hoods or chemical wet stations) for several hours each day
Strong verbal and written communication skills

Qualifications:

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates. This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

Minimum Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering with 4+ years of hands-on experience in Process Integration or Yield Engineering demonstrated through internships, academic projects, coursework, or hands-on training, OR a Master's degree in Chemical Engineering with 2+ years of hands-on experience.

- Familiarity with machine learning techniques and data analytics tools.

- Availability and ability to work on weekends.

Preferred Qualifications

- Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to quickly synthesize complex data into actionable solutions.

- Excellent communication and collaboration abilities to work effectively with cross-functional teams.

- Passion for continuous learning, innovation, and contributing to impactful projects.

Your expertise will drive meaningful improvements in manufacturing and deliver world-class results. Don't miss the chance to be part of a team shaping the future of technology. Apply today.

Job Type:
Experienced Hire

Shift:
Shift 1 (Israel)

Primary Location:
Israel, Kiryat-Gat

Additional Locations:

About Marvell

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

Your Team, Your Impact
Infrastructure Processor Business Unit, a part of Networking and Processor Business Group, encompasses OCTEON and the award-winning OCTEON Fusion-M® product families. The SoC family of multi-core CPU processors and Radio Access SoCs offer best-in-class performance, low power, rich software ecosystem, virtualization features, and open source application support with highly optimized custom ARM CPU cores providing an excellent solution for a highly flexible end-to-end optimized 5G platform.

As part of the Infrastructure Processor unit at Marvell, you will verify all of the circuitry that goes inside our chips for the general market and for specific customers. These chips use cutting-edge technology to facilitate data transfers at high speeds, and you will help verify that each design meets our customers’ specifications whether they’re a major telecom organization or automotive company, etc.

What You Can Expect
In this (hybrid/remote/in-office) role in LOCATION, you’ll work day to day with an RTL engineer to verify their design. Their design is in Verilog; you’ll use System Verilog to debug. You’ll run simulations using Synopsys VCS or a similar program, and then debug as needed until the design meets required specifications. You’ll also work closely with DFT engineers who are working in parallel on your blocks.

You’ll attend weekly staff meetings to go over what everyone is working on and update your progress or address any issues. As you take responsibility for larger blocks, you may have to present to a review committee and explain your test plan and test schedule for those larger blocks.

What We're Looking For

To be successful in this role you must:

- Have completed a Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering and have 2 to 3 years of related professional experience OR a Master’s Degree and/or PhD in those fields.

- Your coursework must have included some analog classes, Verilog or VHDL, basic circuits, and computer architecture. You should have a focus in VLSI or show projects in your courses that directly relate to chip design.

- You have used a tool like Synopsys, Cadence, or Mentor to run simulations and you can write and debug a testbench.

- Be comfortable working in a Linux environment and doing scripting with Python.

- Be extremely detail-oriented and ready to iterate a design over and over again until it is refined completely.

- Work and communicate well with your team, keeping them in the loop about your progress, issues you encounter, and any deviations from the planned schedule.



Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements

With competitive compensation and great benefits, you will enjoy our workstyle within an environment of shared collaboration, transparency, and inclusivity. We’re dedicated to giving our people the tools and resources they need to succeed in doing work that matters, and to grow and develop with us. For additional information on what it’s like to work at Marvell, visit our Careers page.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Interview Integrity

To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.

These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.

This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.

Description
What we are looking for

Nova Israel Finance Team is seeking for a talented and experience Purchase to Pay & Inventory Manager .

In this role, you will be responsible for overseeing financial workflows related to inventory control, supply chain accounting, vendor relationships, procurement analysis and other areas. This is an exceptional opportunity for a Big-4 alumnus to transition into a dynamic corporate environment and take major ownership of vital financial operations.

You will join the Israel Accounting team, based at Nova's headquarters in Israel.

The team consists of approximately 15 finance professionals, responsible for the financial operations and reporting of Nova's Israeli entity, with annual revenues of approximately $600M.

Role Responsibilities
What will you be doing:

- Lead all accounting and operational finance activities related to Nova Israel's inventory.

- Manage the team responsible for inventory financial management, closing, and reporting.

- Collaborate with Operations and provide accounting guidance on inventory maintenance and recording.

- Oversee the purchasing-to-payment process, including accounting, invoicing, and payment matters related to supplier purchase orders and agreements.

- Manage accounts payable through designated bookkeepers, including ongoing maintenance, quarter-end aging, and reconciliations.

- Oversee capital asset purchases and fixed asset module accounting, including approvals, management, and closing processes.

- Manage lease accounting, including approvals, ongoing management, and closing processes.

- Perform analytical reviews of OPEX and Israel's financial statements.

- Handle bank-related activities and review hedging processes.

- Support ongoing financial operations and quarter-end closing assignments under the guidance of the Accounting and Control Manager.

- Support and execute SOX processes related to the above areas.

Requirements
Must Have:

- Certified Public Accountant (CPA), with at least 5 years of post-internship experience.

- At least 5 years of experience as a Controller in a business company.

- Proven experience managing a small team of junior accountants or bookkeepers.

- Experience in the high-tech sector within a Big 4 accounting firm.

- Strong knowledge of US GAAP, including inventory and manufacturing accounting principles.

- Experience with SOX compliance.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

- Strong Excel proficiency and analytical capabilities.

Advantages

- Experience handling complex accounting matters.

- Hands-on experience with Oracle ERP systems.

- Experience working in a global, publicly traded high-tech company.

That special something you bring in:

- Strong ownership and ability to independently lead areas of responsibility from A to Z.

- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

- Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple teams and organizational levels.

Get to know us better:

Nova (NASDAQ: NVMI) is a global company and a leading provider of innovative metrology solutions for process control in semiconductor manufacturing.

With a team of ~1200 people in three R&D centers and 27 field offices, we bring insights into the world’s most advanced industry. We leverage multiple technology fields such as physics, optics, chemistry, and algorithms to develop hardware and software solutions that measure almost every advanced computer chip built in the world.

Nova dives deep into dimensions and layers at the atomic level to extract unique insights and provide our customers with crucial decision-making data, managing critical challenges by providing unique, differentiated solutions.

Our outstanding people-focused and innovative culture means every person at Nova has the power to make an impact and significantly redefine what people can achieve through technology.

Join us if you are

A dreamer and brilliant high aimer who sees the impossible as the starting point and loves working in a multidisciplinary global team to create innovative breakthroughs.

If you need assistance due to a disability, you may contact us at talent@novami.com

title: סטודנט/ית למחלקת כספים

description:
We’re looking for a Computer / Electrical engineering student to join our IoT Validation & Automation team.

You’ll help operate our hardware validation lab and grow into building the automation that powers end-to-end HW/FW testing across Augury’s IoT platforms.

You’ll work hands-on with real lab equipment, write and extend Python/Robot Framework tests, and collaborate with Hardware, Embedded Firmware, Linux, and System Engineering. No prior industry experience is required — we care about strong fundamentals, curiosity, and the drive to learn in a real production lab.

What you’ll do Support IoT hardware test and validation: automated tests, diagnostic tooling, and lab processes.

Help maintain lab infrastructure: test benches, measurement equipment, calibration workflows, and tools.

Operate lab assets such as SpectraQuest rigs, magnetic

Helmholtz coils, power analyzers, and RF chambers — with mentorship.

Execute regression, stress, performance, and multi-revision hardware tests as part of the validation pipeline.

Develop and maintain automated end-to-end test scripts (Python, Robot Framework). Contribute to lab automation software and pipelines (Python, Jenkins, Docker, Git). Work with automation infrastructure: APIs, SSH interfaces, databases, and CI/CD flows.

Help validate gateways, sensors, mobile, connectivity, and HW/FW integration scenarios.

Work with hardware, firmware, software, and system engineers on validation workflows.

Write and improve lab procedures, validation notes, and equipment documentation.

Support root-cause investigations and reliability improvements.

What you bring

Currently studying Computer Engineering / Electrical Engineering. At least 3 semesters remaining before graduation.

Comfortable working AI-native: uses

AI coding/assistant tools as part of how you learn, write, and debug — while still owning the fundamentals.

Solid software fundamentals:

Python preferred (scripting / OOP coursework or personal projects). Coursework or strong interest in signal processing, sensors, or embedded/IoT systems.

Comfort learning Linux/Unix, command-line tools, and SSH. Interest in networking and wireless concepts (Wi-Fi, BLE, cellular — classroom level is fine). Curiosity about physical hardware and lab work; willingness to learn electronic test equipment.

Strong problem-solving, attention to detail, and ability to work independently with guidance. No prior industry experience required.

Nice to have Academic lab experience (electronics, DSP, communications, or mechatronics labs). Familiarity with test automation ideas or frameworks (Robot Framework or similar). Knowledge of IoT-related protocols:

BLE, MQTT, SSH. Personal projects involving hardware, Raspberry Pi/Arduino, sensors, or automation scripts.

Any exposure to CI tools (Jenkins, GitHub Actions) or containers (Docker). Technologies you’ll work with Python, Robot Framework, Patrol, Jenkins, Docker, SSH, Git, Postman, MongoDB, Google Cloud Platform, Azure, logic analyzers, RF chambers, Helmholtz coils, spectra/vibration analyzers, power analyzers, and other electronic test equipment.

Benefits Hybrid student role in Haifa (~100 hours/month, 2 days in office + remote). Hands-on exposure to industrial IoT hardware and real validation infrastructure.

Mentorship from experienced validation and automation engineers.

Meaningful ownership of automation work that ships into CI and lab practice. A path to grow into advanced validation, automation, and systems roles. To apply

Please include your CV, grades transcript, and a short note on relevant coursework, lab work, signal-processing/software projects, or personal automation projects.

Basic qualifications
- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent

Preferred qualifications
- 5+ years of embedded firmware development experience

- 5+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
